data.body:
Second merge of B-export-surfaces (split by exp8-surfaces to keep hot files short-held). The first merge gives list/print/--diff/--out/--check/--update/--force/--all, --template, [export] config, shared-glob registration and the MCP ddflow_export (list/print/write). This task adds, per D-export-selection, D-export-agent-enable and D-export-templates:
- `ddflow export enable <doc> [--path P] [--mode whole|region|append] [--local]`, `disable <doc> [--lock]`, `ack`; MCP actions enable/disable; guarded config write like config --set; an enable creates no file.
- Agent enable: allowed without approval, always visible (result names the agent and the stop command), export.enabled / export.disabled optional event kinds (core/model.py; forward-compat B1c4a2346a9) with agent, document, path, mode, time, locked; `ddflow export` lists who enabled each and when; brief line until acknowledged (`ddflow export` at a TTY or `export ack`); doctor note; `disable --lock` makes a later agent enable exit 3; unlocking is operator-only (refused under --agent/DDFLOW_AGENT/CLAUDECODE like reviewers approve).
- `ddflow export eject <doc>` (.ddflow/templates/export/<kind>.md.j2, idempotent, --force; records the shipped-template digest), `ddflow export validate [<doc>]` (template errors with file and line; note when an ejected copy is older than the shipped default); MCP validate; doctor note on template drift.
Acceptance (failing-first): as in the appended blocks D-export-selection / D-export-agent-enable / D-export-templates of B-export-surfaces.

chunk_findings.detail:
`export_tool` is written to let an MCP caller diff/check an arbitrary repo-relative file:

```python
if path and not (write or diff or check):
    return O.refused(...)
```
and its docstring states: "``path`` without ``write`` is refused (exit 3) unless it is the target of a ``diff`` or ``check``". It then forwards `out=path` together with `diff=diff` / `check=check`. But `export` immediately rejects that combination:

```python
if sum(map(bool, (diff, check, update, out))) > 1:
    raise ExportError("--diff, --check, --update and --out are alternatives", EXIT_REFUSED)
```

Concrete input: `ddflow_export(doc="roadmap", path="docs/roadmap.md", diff=true)`. The pre-checks pass (path with `diff` is allowed), then `export(..., diff=True, out="docs/roadmap.md", ...)` hits the guard, returns exit 3 with "…are alternatives", and no diff is ever produced. Same for `check=true` + `path`. The same diff shows the dead giveaway: `_act` explicitly supports this case (`ops.write_doc(..., target=out, check=check, diff=diff, ...)` in the `if diff or check:` branch) — that `target=out` is unreachable because the guard forbids `out` together with `diff`/`check`. So either the guard must not count `out` when it is being used as the compare target, or `export_tool` must not pass `out=path` for diff/check; as written, the MCP action the tool advertises cannot be invoked. (The CLI cannot hit this, so it is also an MCP-parity break.)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/export.py — `export_tool` (`export_tool`) vs `export` (the `--diff/--check/--update/--out are alternatives` guard)

chunk_findings.detail:
The tool's docstring promises "a path is never silently ignored", but the list fallback bypasses every argument check:

```python
doc, every = str(a.get("doc") or ""), bool(a.get("all"))
if not doc and not every:
    return export_list(repo)
```

Concrete input: `ddflow_export(path="docs/x.md")` (or `write=true, path=...`, or `diff=true, path=...`) with no `doc`/`all` returns the `export.list` outcome with exit 0 and silently drops `write`/`path`/`diff`/`check`. A caller asking to operate on a path gets a listing instead of the promised exit-3 refusal; an agent that forgot `doc` cannot tell that nothing it asked for happened.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/export.py — `export_tool` early return

chunk_findings.detail: The `filters` value check claims to enforce "a table of strings and integers", but `int` in a `str | int` union also matches `bool`, since `bool` is a subclass of `int`. So a table like `[export.bugs] filters = { limit = true }` (TOML boolean) passes validation with an empty problem string instead of being rejected, and the boolean is then carried into the config's filter map. Downstream, if `limit` is applied as an integer slice/count, `True` coerces to `1`, so the export is silently truncated to one item rather than reporting the malformed filter — a wrong result from an accepted input. (Note the `redact` check already guards against this via `isinstance(..., bool)`, so the asymmetry is clearly unintended.) Excluding `bool` explicitly (e.g. `isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool)`) would reject the input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config.py `_export_table_problem` (the `filters` validation: `isinstance(v, str | int)`)

chunk_findings.detail:
`ExportConfig.tables` is the per-instance dict that stores the `[export.<doc>]` tables (the method itself reads `self.export.tables.get(k, {})` and writes `self.export.tables[k] = ...`, i.e. it must be a normal dataclass field to survive `dataclasses.asdict`/layering). Because the guard skips *every* name that is in `fields(self.export)`, a config table named `tables` is passed through to the generic knob loop untouched and never reaches the `EXPORT_TABLE_KEYS` filter or `_export_table_problem`. Given

```toml
[export.tables.README]
path = "../../escape.md"
mode = "nonsense"
```

`values["tables"] = {"README": {"path": "../../escape.md", "mode": "nonsense"}}`; `k == "tables"` is in `knobs`, so it lands in `plain` and the loop does `setattr(self.export, "tables", {...})` with no filtering and no validation (there is no `_KNOB_CHECKS["export.tables"]` entry — this hunk only adds `export.refresh`, `export.max_bytes`, `export.documents`). The identical table written the documented way,

```toml
[export.README]
path = "../../escape.md"
mode = "nonsense"
```

is refused (`_export_table_problem` / unknown-key handling), so the guard is bypassable for both file loads and the `config --set export.tables ...` / MCP `ddflow_configure` write path. As a side effect it also *replaces* rather than merges `self.export.tables` (the `{**existing, **clean}` merge is skipped when the whole dict is assigned as a plain knob), so an entry that should be refused or merged is silently installed verbatim.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/config.py — `Config._apply_export_tables` (the `if k in knobs or not isinstance(v, dict)` guard)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config.py — `Config._apply_export_tables` (the `if k in knobs or not isinstance(v, dict)` guard)

chunk_findings.detail: `state_of` assumes that a target path which `Path.exists()` reports as present is also a readable UTF-8 text file. `W._read` is used with an `assert old is not None` guard, which acknowledges that `_read` can return `None`. That `None` case is never handled: the assert raises `AssertionError` (and under `python -O` it is stripped, so the next line `F.split(old)` / `_region_edit(old, ...)` raises `TypeError` on `None`). The only caller that can hit this, `listing` (the `ddflow export` list command), wraps the call in `except ExportError` only, so the `AssertionError`/`OSError` escapes. Concrete input: select a doc via `ddflow export enable <doc>` and let its target file be a non-UTF-8/binary file (or a directory) at that path — e.g. the path collides with an existing blob. `path.exists()` is true, `W._read` returns `None` (or raises `IsADirectoryError`/`OSError`), and the whole `ddflow export` listing aborts with a traceback instead of reporting the file as `hand-edited`. The docstring explicitly claims `hand-edited` "also covers a file that is not ddflow's at all", so this input is in scope. The fix is to catch the read failure (or check `old is None`) and return a `hand-edited`/`stale` state rather than asserting.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/services/export/ops.py: state_of (`old = W._read(path)` / `assert old is not None`)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/ops.py: state_of (`old = W._read(path)` / `assert old is not None`)

chunk_findings.detail: The lambda is `lambda repo, a, agent: _api().export_tool(repo, a)`: it accepts the caller/agent identity the dispatcher hands it and then silently discards it, invoking `export_tool` with only the repo and the raw args. D-export-agent-enable requires the export tool to distinguish an agent caller from a TTY operator (it must record the enabling agent's id, emit the `export.enabled` event with that agent, and refuse operator-only operations such as `disable --lock`/unlock "under --agent/DDFLOW_AGENT/CLAUDECODE"), and the acceptance test "a locked document refuses an agent's enable (exit 3)" plus "recorded with its agent id" both depend on that flag. With the flag dropped, an MCP caller is indistinguishable from an operator: an agent-triggered enable cannot be attributed (so `ddflow export`/`brief` will not name who enabled the doc and the stop-command line has no agent), and an agent can satisfy whatever operator-only check `export_tool` performs by reading an env var rather than the passed flag. Concrete scenario: an agent calls `ddflow_export` with `write=true` on a document an operator locked; the intended result is exit/refusal 3 "locked by the operator", but `export_tool` is called without the agent identity, so the lock is not enforced for this call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py — `ddflow_export` api lambda

chunk_findings.detail: The declared properties are doc/all/since/version/phase/item/status/limit/tag/session/max_bytes/diff/check/write/path — there is no `action` (and no `force`, `lock`, `ack`, or `template`) property. The stated design has the MCP tool expose list/enable/disable actions (plus ack/validate/force/template behavior) with CLI/MCP parity, but nothing in the schema lets a client express those operations; an agent that wants to "ask for a document" (D-export-selection: `enable`/`disable` via MCP) or acknowledge an agent-enabled document has no argument to send and, per this schema, the action can never be requested. Concrete scenario: an agent calls `ddflow_export` to enable `roadmap`; the only expressible call is `doc=roadmap`, which is indistinguishable from the read/print path, so the selection is never changed (and `--all`/`brief` acknowledgement requirements cannot be exercised over MCP at all).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py — `ddflow_export` properties

chunk_findings.detail: The topic says `ddflow export` lists every kind with its default target and, "for the selected ones, its state", then enumerates only `fresh`, `stale`, `hand-edited`, `missing`. The spec for this change (D-export-selection) requires the listing to report the state of *every* kind, with the unselected state named explicitly: "lists every kind with its state (not selected / fresh / stale / hand-edited / missing)", and the default `[export].documents` is `[]`. So on a default checkout `ddflow export` must report each kind as `not selected`, a state the help never mentions and whose existence the phrase "for the selected ones" actively denies. A reader (or agent) with the default empty selection is told that the only reported states are the four file-freshness states, none of which can occur when nothing is selected; the documented state vocabulary cannot describe the default output.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/export.md (the "state" sentence)

chunk_findings.detail: D-export-templates acceptance states that "help topic documents the template variables and filters per kind". This new file is the export help topic, yet it contains no template-variable documentation, no per-kind filter list, and no mention of the `--template PATH` flag, `eject`, or `validate` — nor of the newly added `enable`/`disable`/`ack`/`--lock` selection-and-agent-enable commands. Concretely: a user who reads the "Writing" section is told `--all` "does nothing and says so (exit 2)" because the selection is empty, and the topic gives no command (`ddflow export enable <doc>`) to change that; the only path it shows is hand-editing `[export].documents`. The documented surface for these features exists only as an example config block, which will not satisfy the "document … per kind" acceptance or the exit-2 dead end it creates.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/export.md

chunk_findings.detail: The final assertion, `before = (proj / "ROADMAP.md").read_text(); assert before == (proj / "ROADMAP.md").read_text()  # neither wrote`, is a tautology placed *after* the operations it is meant to guard. Both `api.export_documents(proj, "roadmap", check=True)` and `api.export_documents(proj, "roadmap", diff=True)` have already run before `before` is captured, so `before` already reflects any write those calls performed; the two consecutive reads then compare the file to itself with no intervening operation and can never differ. Given a defective implementation in which `--diff` (or `--check`) writes `ROADMAP.md`, this test still passes, so the acceptance requirement that `--diff`/`--check` "neither wrote" is not actually enforced. To exercise it, the content must be snapshotted before the `check`/`diff` calls and compared afterward.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_ops.py::test_check_exit_one_when_stale_and_diff_shows_the_change

chunk_findings.detail:
`export_tool` deliberately accepts `path` together with `diff`/`check`: after the early `if not doc and not every: return export_list(...)`, it only refuses a bare path via `if path and not (write or diff or check)`, and the docstring states that a path "without `write` is refused (exit 3) unless it is the target of a `diff` or `check`". It then forwards that path as `out=path` into `export()`. But `export()` starts with

    if sum(map(bool, (diff, check, update, out))) > 1:
        raise ExportError("--diff, --check, --update and --out are alternatives", EXIT_REFUSED)

so `out` is *always* refused together with `diff` or `check`. Concrete input: an MCP call `ddflow_export({"doc": "roadmap", "check": true, "path": "docs/roadmap.md"})` passes `export_tool`'s guard, reaches `export(doc="roadmap", check=True, out="docs/roadmap.md")`, and the sum is 2, so it returns exit 3 "…are alternatives" instead of checking the document against `docs/roadmap.md`. The same holds for `{"doc": ..., "diff": true, "path": ...}`. This also makes the `target=out` argument in `_act`'s `if diff or check:` branch dead code: that branch can never be reached with a non-empty `out`, since the guard in `export()` has already raised. Either the guard (or `export_tool`'s mapping of `path`) has to change so the documented "path as diff/check target" case actually works.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/api/export.py — `export()` alternatives guard vs `export_tool()` path handling
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/export.py — `export()` alternatives guard vs `export_tool()` path handling

chunk_findings.detail: `state_of` first checks `path.exists()` and then does `old = W._read(path)` followed by `assert old is not None`. The assert is itself an admission that `_read` is optional (`str | None`), and the only states this module is allowed to produce are fresh/stale/hand-edited/missing. Two concrete inputs break that: (a) a non-UTF-8/binary file sitting at the configured target (e.g. someone drops a `.png` or a Latin-1 hand edit on `[export.<doc>].path`) — `exists()` is true, `_read` cannot decode and returns `None`; (b) the file is deleted by another process between the `exists()` call and the read (TOCTOU interleaving). In both cases the resulting `AssertionError` propagates out of `state_of`, and `listing` only wraps the call in `except ExportError` (ops.py listing), so it is not converted to a `("hand-edited"/"missing", detail)` row — `ddflow export` dies with a traceback instead of listing the state, which is exactly the case the docstring promises to fold into `hand-edited` ("a file that is not ddflow's at all"). The read should be handled (`if old is None: return "hand-edited"/"missing", ...`) rather than asserted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/ops.py:state_of (`assert old is not None`)

chunk_findings.detail: `interactive = bool(a.update and not a.yes and sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty())` ignores `c.json`, so the confirm callback is handed to `A.export` even when machine output was requested. `_confirm` writes the diff and the `Write <rel>? [y/N] ` prompt to stdout, and only *after* `A.export` returns does the CLI do `print(json.dumps(out.body(), indent=2, default=str))` to the same stream. Concretely, running `ddflow --json export <doc> --update` in a terminal (no `--yes`) produces stdout consisting of the unified diff plus `Write ...? [y/N] ` followed by the JSON document, which is not parseable as JSON — exactly the `--json`/MCP-parity path that is supposed to be machine-readable. The prompt (or the whole confirm path) needs to be suppressed when `c.json` is set, or routed to stderr.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/export.py:cmd_export (the `interactive`/`confirm` wiring)

chunk_findings.detail: The D-export-templates acceptance explicitly requires that "help topic documents the template variables and filters per kind", and the CLI surface includes `ddflow export eject <doc>` and `ddflow export <doc> --template PATH`. The new help topic contains no mention of templates whatsoever: the word "template" never appears, the config example under `[export.<doc>]` lists only `path`, `mode`, `filters` (the mandated `template` key is omitted), `--template`/`eject`/`validate` are not described, and there is no per-kind variable/filter reference. A failing-first test that asserts the mandated help content (e.g. that `ddflow help export` documents `--template`, `eject`, `validate`) fails against this file, and an operator/agent reading the shipped help cannot discover the template workflow at all.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/export.md (template documentation, absent)

chunk_findings.detail: D-export-selection makes selection the primary gate ("nothing generated unless selected") and defines `ddflow export enable <doc> [--path P] [--mode whole|region|append] [--local]`, `disable <doc>`, and `ack`; D-export-agent-enable adds `disable --lock` and the operator-only unlock rule. The help topic documents none of these words; the only way it shows to populate the default-empty `[export].documents` is editing the config by hand, so `ddflow help export` cannot answer how to select a document. It also states the state list as showing state only "for the selected ones" (`fresh`/`stale`/`hand-edited`/`missing`) and never mentions the mandated `not selected` state, so a user cannot tell which of the default-empty selection is even eligible for `--all`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/export.md (## The kinds / ## Writing)

chunk_findings.detail:
The guard intended to prove that `--check` / `--diff` do not write is a tautology:

```python
before = (proj / "ROADMAP.md").read_text()
assert before == (proj / "ROADMAP.md").read_text()  # neither wrote
```

`before` is read *after* both `api.export_documents(..., check=True)` and `api.export_documents(..., diff=True)` have already run, so both sides of the comparison are the same file read twice in a row and the assertion can never fail. If the diff/check path were to (re)write `ROADMAP.md` — e.g. sharing the write path with `--update` — this test would still pass, so the "check and diff never write" property is untested. The snapshot must be taken before the `chk`/`d` calls and compared afterwards.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_ops.py:183-184 (`test_check_exit_one_when_stale_and_diff_shows_the_change`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The test is named "maps **or** is refused", but the "maps" branch asserts nothing:

```python
out = api.export_documents(proj, "roadmap", version="0.1.0")
if "version" not in {f.name for f in fields(Filters)}:
    assert out.exit == 3 and "version" in out.reason
```

When `Filters` does declare a `version` field (i.e. the filter is supported and must filter the roadmap), the whole body of the `if` is skipped and no check of `out.exit` or of the produced text is performed at all. In exactly the case the test claims to cover — version mapping to a working filter — a completely broken implementation (e.g. `version="0.1.0"` returning exit 3 or an unfiltered document) passes the test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_ops.py:129-132 (`test_version_filter_maps_or_is_refused`)

chunk_findings.detail: The acceptance is "no new dependency", but the enforcement only walks three files: `services/export/ops.py`, `api/export.py`, `surfaces/commands/export.py`. The export package has other modules that the test itself imports — `ddflow/services/export/registry.py` (`R`) and `ddflow/services/export/write.py` (`W`) — and none of them (nor any render module) is inspected. Concretely, adding `import tabulate` at the top of `ddflow/services/export/registry.py` leaves this test green while violating the stated "no new dependency" acceptance; the file list needs to cover the whole export package (glob the directory) rather than a hand-picked three.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_ops.py:317-326 (`test_no_dependency_beyond_the_standard_library_and_jinja`)

chunk_findings.detail: The stated acceptance criterion for this change is that the new tool "must stay within the tools/list byte budget (tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py) and its tier." This diff does not make `ddflow_export` fit that budget — it moves the budget. Concretely: the comment itself records that `main` sat at 91,958 bytes against a 92,000-byte limit, and that `ddflow_export` adds ~1.4 KB (15 arguments), i.e. roughly 91,958 + ~1,430 ≈ 93,39x bytes. With the old constant (92_000) the schema is over budget by ~1.4 KB and the check fails; with the new constant (93_500) it passes. So the one guard that was supposed to bound this change is edited by the change, and nothing else bounds it — the 15-argument schema (which the comment attributes to flag-parity completeness) can grow unbounded as long as each commit also bumps the constant. If the intended constraint is "the tool fits in the budget", the check should have been reproduced against 92_000 (e.g. by trimming the schema, folding the filter flags into a single string argument as is done for `ddflow_import`'s `relation`, or adding the tool to the cheaper read surface) rather than by raising the threshold in the same commit that consumes the headroom.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py:15 (TOOLS_LIST_BUDGET)

titles: ddflow/api/export.py — `export()` alternatives guard vs `export_tool()` path handling

chunk_findings.detail: The refactor drops the unknown-filter guard entirely. The old body computed `names = {f.name for f in fields(R.Filters)}`, raised `ExportError(..., EXIT_REFUSED)` for any non-falsy key not in `names`, and then constructed `R.Filters(**{k: v for k, v in kw.items() if k in names ...})`. The new body forwards every non-falsy key straight through: `given = {k: v for k, v in {**kw, "tag": tag or version}.items() if v not in ("", 0, None)}` then `R.Filters(**given)`. `R.Filters` is a dataclass (the old code called `dataclasses.fields` on it), so its generated `__init__` rejects unknown keywords with `TypeError`, not a controlled refusal. Concrete input: any caller that spreads a filter mapping containing a key this build's `Filters` does not know — e.g. an MCP call whose `filters` object carries an extra/future key, which is exactly the forward-compat case the surrounding change is meant to tolerate — now reaches `R.Filters(**given)` and raises `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument '...'` instead of the previous `ExportError` with `EXIT_REFUSED` (exit 1). The user-visible contract changes from "refused, exit 1, with the list of accepted filters" to an uncaught traceback / wrong exit code. Note also that keeping `**kw` in the signature while removing the only thing that validated `kw` means the parameter is now an unchecked hole into `R.Filters`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/export.py:_filters

chunk_findings.detail: The old append path built its producer with `_produce(repo, cfg, q, spec, template)`, which captured the resolved `template` and rendered the appended entries through `_body(repo, cfg, sub, spec, template)` — i.e. the template selection (ad-hoc `--template PATH` or `[export.<doc>] template`) was honored for append-mode documents. The new path calls `appender(spec.doc)` (whose factory signature is `append_unreleased(query)`, returning `produce(last)`) and then `make(q)`, passing only the query. Neither the factory nor the produced callable receives `template` (nor `spec`), so the template is silently dropped for append writes. Concrete input: `ddflow export changelog --out CHANGELOG.md --template my.j2` (changelog is described as the append kind), or a `[export.changelog] template = ...` config entry — before this change the appended entries were rendered with `my.j2`; now they are rendered with the kind's built-in template and `my.j2` is silently ignored, so the file content written to the target differs from what the user requested. If append mode is not meant to accept templates, it should be refused rather than silently ignored.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/ops.py (`write_doc`, append branch: `make = appender(spec.doc)` / `make(q)`)
ddflow/api/export.py:_filters

chunk_findings.detail:
`_export_tables_problem` validates that the container passed for `[export].tables` is a dict, but it never validates that each *value* is itself a table before delegating, even though its docstring promises "each value is a valid `[export.<doc>]` table". The `isinstance(t, dict)` test only guards the unknown-key branch; a non-dict value falls straight through to `_export_table_problem(str(doc), t)`. That delegate is written against a mapping — its body does `"redact" in t`, `t["redact"]`, `t["filters"].items()` — and it is only ever reached from the sub-table path, where unknown scalar keys under `[export]` are tolerated as forward-compat, so it has no non-dict guard. Concretely, with

```toml
[export]
tables = { changelog = 1 }
```

`t` is `1`, the `isinstance(t, dict)` branch is skipped, and `_export_table_problem("changelog", 1)` evaluates `"redact" in 1`, raising `TypeError: argument of type 'int' is not iterable` instead of returning a "must be a table" message — config loading / `config --set` validation blows up with a traceback. With a string value (`tables = { changelog = "docs/x.md" }`) it is worse: `"redact" in t` and `"filters" in t` are plain substring tests that are both false, so the function returns `""` and a scalar is silently accepted as a document table, violating the stated rule. An element-level `isinstance(t, dict)` check is missing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config.py:_export_tables_problem

chunk_findings.detail:
The new test asserts that a table containing an *unknown* key must be rejected:

```python
for bad in (
    {"R": {"mode": "nonsense"}},
    {"R": {"path": "x", "nope": 1}},          # <-- unknown key
    {"R": {"filters": {"limit": True}}},
    "not a table",
):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        Config.check({"export": {"tables": bad}})
```

But the change's own requirement for this section is forward-compatibility with unknown keys (“`[export]` config section (… `[export.<doc>]` path/mode/template/filters) with forward-compat for unknown keys”). Given a config authored by a newer ddflow that adds a key to a document table — e.g. `Config.check({"export": {"tables": {"R": {"path": "x", "nope": 1}}}})`, or equally the user-facing `[export.roadmap]` with a future `nope = 1` — this test encodes that the current version must raise `ValueError` rather than ignore the unknown key. Whichever way the implementation is written, the change is wrong: if the implementation follows the asserted behaviour, an older binary hard-fails on a forward-compatible config (violating the stated requirement); if it is forward-compatible as required, this test fails. The `nope` case is not a type/range error (unlike `mode: nonsense` or `limit: True`), so it is exactly the forward-compat case that the surrounding code is supposed to tolerate, which is why this expectation should not be asserted.
